title: Annual Accounts
summary: The ECB published its Annual Accounts for 2025 on February 26, 2026, reporting a balance sheet contraction of €37.3 billion to €603.3 billion, driven primarily by the cessation of reinvestments under its asset purchase programmes. The ECB recorded a loss of €1,254 million, significantly lower than 2024, due to decreased interest expense from the net TARGET liability.
key_points: ECB balance sheet contracted by €37.3 billion in 2025, reaching €603.3 billion
Contraction was mainly due to declining monetary policy securities as the Eurosystem stopped reinvesting principal payments from maturing APP securities
ECB recorded a loss of €1,254 million for 2025, substantially lower than 2024 losses
Loss reduction was driven by decreased interest expense from net TARGET liability
Losses will remain on balance sheet to be offset against future profits
Annual Accounts are published each February as part of the ECB's Annual Report
why_it_matters: This retrospective financial accounting document provides transparency on the ECB's balance sheet trajectory during ongoing QT. The €37.3 billion contraction reflects the mechanical unwind of QE-era holdings, while the TARGET liability interest expense continues to represent a structural cost of TARGET2 imbalances within the euro system. These figures are backward-looking and do not directly signal near-term policy changes.
macro_context: The balance sheet contraction reflects the ECB's passive QT through ceased APP reinvestments. The loss attributable to TARGET liability interest expense relates to cross-border payment imbalances within the euro area. These are accounting outcomes of prior policy decisions, not forward-looking indicators.
market_structure_context: The mention of TARGET liability relates to TARGET2, the European retail payment infrastructure. Interest expenses on TARGET balances reflect the cost of cross-border settlement within the euro payment system, though this Annual Accounts document does not detail operational aspects of market plumbing.
